comment:
Source review found incomplete payload-size protection and an incorrect pathname expectation in the added test.

## The 500-file cap is not a byte limit

In [`omarchy-menu-file`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/f4a067bdc858cf3e158e787b539c8f4e9992d9ff/bin/omarchy-menu-file#L47-L57), `head -n 500` limits entries, while `omarchy-menu-select` still passes the entire encoded options array as one argument to Perl and later passes the menu payload through the shell IPC command.

Source-derived example with synthetic path lengths, not a runtime reproduction:

```text
500 paths × 280 ASCII bytes = 140,000 bytes before JSON overhead
                              > 131,072-byte single-argument limit
```

**Impact:** On Linux systems with that argument limit, a collection of sufficiently long paths can still fail with an argument-too-long error instead of opening the picker. The cap helps ordinary-length collections but does not guarantee the protection stated in the comment.

**Suggested change:** Bound the encoded payload size with room for metadata, or use a transport that avoids a single oversized argument at both the Perl and shell/IPC boundaries.

**Test-only correction:** [`menu-file-symlink-test.sh:26`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/f4a067bdc858cf3e158e787b539c8f4e9992d9ff/test/shell.d/menu-file-symlink-test.sh#L26) expects `$real/clip.webm`, but `find -L` traverses the symlink without canonicalizing `%p`:

```text
starting point: $link -> $real
emitted path:   $link/clip.webm
test expects:  $real/clip.webm
```

By source inspection, this assertion rejects the intended output and makes the new test fail. Compare with `"$link/clip.webm"` instead. This is a test expectation mismatch, not a failure of the symlink traversal fix.

**Verified by source inspection:** `-L` follows symlinked starting directories, newest-first sorting is retained, and the selector's nonzero exit status still propagates. Only the newest 500 matches remain eligible, so older files are omitted from the picker.
